reads.kernelForm:
DELIVERABLE VERIFY-PATH KERNEL FORM = a SEQUENTIAL rank-1 tree-scan whose accepted-chain state is published by a SIBLING replay kernel (NOT chunked-WY, NOT all-rows publish). Concretely it is the SAME object already on HEAD as `_tree_gdn_replay_kernel` + `launch_tree_gdn_replay` (src/lumo_flywheel_serving/fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py:545-846), driven by `STORE_NODE_STATES=False` on the scan (kernel arg at :421, set via `store_node_states=not _fr13_replay_route_on` at scripts/fr10_phase4_patch_vllm_tree_gdn.py:4115).

WHAT IT COMPUTES vs the deployed all-rows kernel:
- The verify SCAN (`_tree_gdn_kernel`, :386-543) is UNCHANGED math — sequential rank-1 per ancestor path via the shared `_gdn_node_step` body (:337-383), h_cache registers, strict-mask isolation, byte-exact-to-native-on-spine, batch-invariant by construction. Its ONLY change is the `if STORE_NODE_STATES:` per-node HBM export at :533-543 is COMPILED OUT (it is pure export — nothing in-kernel reads it; children resume from h_cache registers, confirmed by the in-kernel comment :534-538).
- Instead of materializing all N node states to HBM (the 5.14x / "36 row-touches" tax) and letting the next step pick one, the scan stores each node's tiny INPUTS to an activation ring (k pre-l2norm, v, raw_a, raw_b at consumed precision, ~16 KiB bf16, ~190x smaller per FR13_GDN_KERNEL_LINEAGE.md:6,11).
- After the committer knows the accepted path, `_tree_gdn_replay_kernel` RE-EXECUTES ONLY that accepted chain from h0: `for t in tl.static_range(0, PATH_COLS+1)` (:624), loading each accepted node's ring inputs and calling the IDENTICAL shared `_gdn_node_step` body (:674-688), then publishing post-step states DIRECTLY to the bank's LINEAR columns (dst_col = t-1, :691-706). It carries ONE `(BLOCK_V, DIM_K)` register tile (`state`, :609-616) — NO h_cache.

HOW IT CUTS TRAFFIC: 36 -> 6 row-touches/layer/req = 21.74 -> 3.62 GB/forward = 0.86x ACTUAL native HBM (sub-native); replay compute is free under the ~99 ms weight-bandwidth floor (FR13_GDN_KERNEL_LINEAGE.md:14). SPILL-FREE AT ANY TREE SIZE: the no-h_cache single-register-tile design removes the N_PAD~16 register-spill wall (the +42-46ms/node scaling wall flagged in the WHY-NOW context) — this is the scaling unlock for wide/suffix-decoding trees. Two bit-exactness obligations are baked in: (1) parent-handoff `-0.0 -> +0.0` flip reproduced via `state = state + 0.0` per edge (:645, the scan's tl.where(offs_n==j) sum flips it exactly once); (2) root replays unconditionally even on ZERO-ACCEPT so bank row-0 (which the next h0 read clamps accepted_len-1 -> col 0) is refreshed (:625-631). It runs in the NATIVE gate-folding basis (RAW_GATING=True, no rescaled-exp reconstruction). NOT chunked-WY: per reference_gdn_verify_sequential_dispatch, vLLM Qwen3-Next VERIFY dispatch = fused_sigmoid_gating sequential rank-1; chunked/WY block-math (`fla_chunk_gated_delta_rule`) is PREFILL-only with a ~6e-5 chunk-vs-recurrent gap = never bit-exact for verify (FR13_GDN_KERNEL_LINEAGE.md:21).

1. ACCEPT-ONLY STATE (branch fr13-accept-only-wip 1a566d41, PARKED) = the FIRST attempt: keep the scan exporting all N states but PUBLISH only the accepted path's rows to the durable bank (path-only publish replacing all-rows publish). Its own live page-stomp was fixed (02b1627a). So: accept-only -> replay = STAGE 1 -> STAGE 2 of the SAME kernel.

3. It is NOT a stage of accept-only/replay — it is the LAST-RESORT fallback if the replay route hard-fails. It "naturally" cuts traffic (no all-rows export) but trades away byte-exactness for the within-floor bar.

reads.orderingContract:
The accept-only/replay route must satisfy a strict producer-write-before-consumer-read contract across the step boundary, with bank-convention separation:
(1) PUBLISH SITE = committer (Option 1), AFTER accept is known, BEFORE the next step's forward. launch_tree_gdn_replay (fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py:709) re-executes root+accepted chain from the activation ring and writes post-step ssm states to bank LINEAR columns, ALWAYS refreshing column 0 (zero-accept path). It REPLACES (a) the forward's all-rows ssm_state.index_copy_ publish and (b) the ssm half of the next-step linear remap. Committer wiring at patcher :6123-6179 keys rows by request-id (_LUMO_FA_SAMPLER_ROW_REQ_IDS / _LUMO_FA_SPEC_ROW_REQ_IDS) so a finishing/joining request never replays over the wrong slot (bug-class 1/8 / drift-risk R8).
(2) H0 READ SITE = next event's scan, fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py:333-347, reads h0 at row spec_state_indices[b, clamp(prev_len-1,0)] (clamp :337-340), i.e. the PREVIOUS event's accepted length. CONTRACT: the column the replay wrote at event N (linear column accepted_len-1; column 0 on zero-accept) must be EXACTLY the column the event-N+1 scan clamps to. The replay's prev_len column MUST be derived from the PRE-COMMIT lens snapshot, never the live buffer (the committer overwrites _LUMO_FA_ACCEPTED_TREE_LENS_TENSOR with the NEW lens at patcher :3625-3638 before any publish-site replay runs — drift-risk R1). The build honors this via a SCAN-TIME snapshot copied at fr10_b==0: patcher :4051-4064 (_fr13_replay_prev_lens / _fr13_replay_spec_idx copy_ from _fr10_accepted_lens_tensor / spec_state_indices_tensor BEFORE the committer refill).
(3) BANK-CONVENTION SEPARATION (drift-risk R2): the ssm bank is LINEAR after the replay; the conv bank stays NODE-keyed until the next forward's conv remap. They must NOT be unified. The conv half of the remap is KEPT but rerouted through the page-safe replay_conv_state_linear_remap (patcher :1838-1846) so it copies only conv-view logical elements (the gate-4 page-stomp fix). The conv prior-window read (committed_path_node mode, patcher :1886-1897) reads NODE columns; deleting the conv remap re-creates the FR13 conv-prior-window bug.
(4) WHO READS THE REJECTED-ROW SLOTS: nothing should — rejected node columns are provably dead once the linear publish lands; under all-rows publish they happened to be refreshed, under accept-only they are left as the previous occupant's bytes, which is SAFE only because (a) the scan reads h0 from the accepted (linear) column, not a rejected node column, and (b) the conv remap touches only the conv slice. The page-stomp violated (b); that was the bug.
(5) NO PER-STEP ALLOCS / DICTS inside the captured region (bug-class 6 / drift-risk R3): all ring/snapshot/flag buffers are preallocated at GDN metadata-builder init (patcher :309-554); the freshness handshake is a preallocated int32 _fr13_replay_flags tensor written by captured device fill_ ([0]=fresh, [1]=staged spec-decode rows, patcher :4075-4078), so a graph REPLAY re-arms freshness without Python re-running.

reads.offlineMissReason: Offline single-forward bit-identical (gate 2: accepted-row publish vs old publish max_abs 0.0; Gate A: replay-vs-scan durable bank bytes 126/126 incl two-event synthetic, 48-layer sweep) structurally CANNOT see the live carrier for three reasons. (1) WRONG INTERVAL: the gates proved everything up to the PRODUCER's bank bytes (event N write) and assumed the consumer reads those same bytes; the defect lived entirely in the INTERVAL between producer-write and consumer-read — an intervening writer (the page-stomping conv remap) overwrote the just-published bytes BETWEEN steps. A single forward never exercises that interval; a two-event synthetic only exercises it if it co-allocates the conv/ssm page-sharing view, which the offline harness did not (it used isolated state banks, not the live as_strided page-shared kv-cache). (2) HISTORY-DEPENDENT garbage: the stomped-in bytes are page leftovers (boot-fresh zeros vs reused-block), so the corruption is non-deterministic and ONLY appears under live multi-request block-pool churn — invisible to a deterministic offline replay. (3) LIVE-ONLY actors uncovered offline: the native mamba_utils copy paths (get_temporal_copy_spec, R6g) and REQKEY/ring churn (R8) only fire across real scheduler steps. This is bug-class 8 ("offline single-forward != live multi-step", now PROVEN THREE times: original accept-only f8ad5f92, replay 9d4d22e3, and resolved at 02b1627a). The methodological fix is baked into the plan: every gate after Gate A is LIVE multi-step (B=1 same-seed repeat first, then the publish-before-next-h0-read boundary join, then the 3-arm corruption gate, then B=4 capture), and the boundary instrument captures the consumer's input AS-READ vs producer's output AS-WRITTEN so the diff NAMES the interval actor instead of just flagging a downstream symptom.
